newsitem.title: USA: Federal Reserve rate hikes not warranted - Saxton.
newsitem.headline: Federal Reserve rate hikes not warranted - Saxton.

text.p: Federal Reserve interest rate increases rates are not justified by the modest increases in inflation shown in March's Consumer Price Index, Congressional Joint Economic Committee Chairman Jim Saxton, a New Jersey Republican, said Tuesday.
"In the absence of inflation signals reflected in the CPI, commodity markets, the value of the dollar, or bond market, Federal Reserve hikes in interest rates are not warranted," he said.
The Labor Department reported the Consumer Price Index rose a modest 0.1 percent in March while the core rate, which excludes food and energy costs, rose 0.2 percent.

Saxton said the rate rise by the Fed last month has introduced uncertainty about the future conduct of monetary policy and Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan should act quickly to "dispel this uncertainty by clearly stating the objective of monetary policy and how it will be implemented."
